papers.title: Association Between Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Longitudinal Glycemic Outcomes in Youth with Type 1 Diabetes.
papers.abstract: AIMS: To investigate the associations of peak and submaximal cardiorespiratory fitness capacity with short- and long-term glycemic outcomes in youth with type 1 diabetes, assessed using continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics and longitudinal HbA1c data from type 1 diabetes onset. METHODS: This secondary analysis of pooled clinical trials data included 77 youth (40 females) with type 1 diabetes who underwent cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). We obtained CGM data from the preceding 90 days to assess short-term glycemic outcome and longitudinal HbA1c data from diagnosis to CPET for assessing long-term cumulative glycemic exposure. We used multivariable regression analyses for evaluating associations with fitness capacity outcomes. RESULTS: Median age was 15.8 years (IQR 14.4-19.5), and type 1 diabetes duration was 8 years (IQR 5.2-11.9). Cumulative glycemic exposure was 68.7%·years (IQR 44.0-101.3), mean time in tight range (TITR) was 42.7 ± 10.7%, and time in range (TIR) was 66.9 ± 11.9%. Median peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) was 39.1 mL/(kg·min) (IQR 34.8-44.9), median first ventilatory threshold (VT1) was 23.1 mL/(kg·min) (IQR 18.0-29.0), and median peak power output (Ppeak) was 3.1 W/kg (IQR 2.8-3.6).Higher cumulative glycemic exposure was independently associated with lower VO2peak (β = -0.053, P = 0.024), VT1 (β = -0.064, P = 0.024), and Ppeak (β = -0.0086, P < 0.001), and greater TITR was independently associated with higher VT1 (β = 0.289 mL/(kg·min) per percentage point, P = 0.003) and higher VT1 expressed as a percentage of VO2peak (β = 0.575, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Better long-term glycemic outcomes were associated with higher aerobic capacity, while favorable short-term glycemic outcomes were specifically associated with a higher submaximal ventilatory threshold. papers.title: Streptomyces qujingensis sp. nov., a novel actinobacterium with broad-spectrum antifungal potential isolated from tobacco rhizosphere soil.
papers.abstract: Strain 144 T, a Gram-positive actinobacterium was isolated from tobacco rhizosphere collected from tobacco fields in Qujing City, Yunnan Province, China (26° 13' 12″ N, 104° 06' 18″ E), and was characterised by a polyphasic taxonomic approach. Comparative 16 S rRNA gene sequencing analysis revealed that strain 144 T belongs to the genus Streptomyces, forming a distinct branch of the phylogenetic tree. Genomic tree analysis indicated close relationships with the type strains of Streptomyces sediminimaris, Streptomyces spinosirectus, Streptomyces plumbidurans, and Streptomyces spinosisporus. The draft genome size of strain 144 T is 10.1 Mbp, with a DNA G + C content of 71.2%. Digital DNA-DNA hybridisation (dDDH), average nucleotide identity (ANI), and average amino acid identity (AAI) values with related strains were well below the species thresholds (70%, 95%, 95%), confirming its genomic distinctness. Morphologically, strain 144 T produces long or slightly curved aerial hyphae that differentiate into rod-shaped spores bearing spiny surfaces. Growth occurs at 10-40 °C, pH 4.0-11.0, and 0-8% NaCl (w/v). Chemotaxonomically, LL-diaminopimelic acid was the diagnostic diamino acid, glucose was the predominant whole-cell sugar, major menaquinones were MK-9(H4), MK-9(H6), and MK-9(H8), and dominant fatty acids included iso-C14:0, anteiso-C15:0, C16:0, iso-C16:0, anteiso-C17:0, and cyclo-C17:0. The polar lipid profile comprised phosphatidylethanolamine, hydroxyphosphatidylethanolamine, diphosphatidylglycerol, phosphatidylglycerol, phosphatidylinositol, phosphatidylinositol mannoside, six unidentified phospholipids, and one unidentified glycolipid. Collectively, the genotypic, phenotypic, and chemotaxonomic data demonstrate that strain 144 T represents a novel species within the genus Streptomyces. papers.title: Benzotriazole UV-stabilizers Induce Warburg-like Metabolic Shift Accompanied by Mitochondrial OXPHOS Impairment.
papers.abstract: Benzotriazole UV stabilizers (BUVs) are globally detected yet their hepatic metabolic toxicity remains undefined. Using human HepG2 cells and integrated in vitro-in silico analyses, we demonstrate that sub-lethal 5 μM BUVs (UV-320, UV-327, UV-328) elicit a biphasic metabolic response: a 24-h ATP surge followed by 48-h collapse, concomitant with suppression of oxygen consumption rate. At the functional level, all congeners suppressed the catalytic activities of Complexes I-V of the mitochondrial electron-transport chain, with UV-327 exhibiting the most severe pan-complex suppression. In silico analysis, including density functional theory calculations and molecular docking, suggested that the 5-chloro substituent in UV-327 may enhance cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV) binding via a π-σ halogen bond, in addition to the hydrogen bonding and π-π stacking interactions commonly observed for all three congeners. Density functional theory-derived Fukui indices and a narrowed HOMO-LUMO gap are consistent with the superior reactivity of UV-327. Accompanying this, cells shifted from oxidative phosphorylation to aerobic glycolysis, evidenced by lactate accumulation and increased enzymatic activities of hexokinase and phosphofructokinase. These findings suggest a novel dual-action mechanism, oxidative phosphorylation impairment coupled with glycolytic shift, underscoring the need for re-evaluating regulatory thresholds for BUVs.

papers.title: Youth perspectives on tuberculosis prevention in South Africa: A qualitative study in faith-based organisations.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading public health challenge in South Africa, with high rates of co-infection with HIV. Faith-based organisations (FBOs) have untapped potential to support TB prevention, particularly by engaging youth who are often overlooked. This study explored youth perspectives on TB prevention and FBOs' roles in advancing youth-led, culturally grounded health promotion strategies in Johannesburg, South Africa. A qualitative, exploratory study was conducted using five focus group discussions with youth aged 18-30 years from Christian, Muslim, and Rastafarian faith communities. The study was guided by principles of Community-Based Participatory Research and Human-Centered Design, applying the 'Define' and 'Develop' phases of the Double Diamond model. Data were analysed using thematic analysis. Participants demonstrated a blend of biomedical knowledge and persistent TB myths. Youth identified FBOs as trusted yet underutilised platforms and proposed strategies including music, storytelling, drama, peer-led health clubs, and digital campaigns. They expressed readiness to lead within faith institutions but noted barriers, including resistance from traditional hierarchies and limited resources. Youth in faith communities possess the creativity, insight, and commitment to transform TB prevention efforts. Strengthening partnerships between youth and FBOs, and investing in participatory, faith-aligned health promotion models, could yield more equitable and sustainable public health outcomes in high-burden settings.

papers.title: Complex IV maturation coordinates postnatal mitochondrial and metabolic development.
papers.abstract: The perinatal heart undergoes a rapid metabolic transition from glycolysis to fatty acid oxidation that requires extensive mitochondrial remodeling, yet the molecular checkpoints that coordinate this process remain poorly defined. Using temporally resolved proteomics and complexome profiling of developing mouse hearts from late gestation through early postnatal life (E18.5 to P10), we identify a discrete developmental window in which respiratory chain architecture is remodeled to enable metabolic commitment. Complex IV (CIV) emerges as a central structural determinant of this transition, undergoing isoform-specific reassembly and transient suppression at birth before incorporation into mature respiratory supercomplexes. We identify the CIV subunit COX7C as a developmentally regulated determinant of CIV maturation, with its abundance increasing during maximal respirasome assembly and the switch to fatty acid oxidation. Loss of COX7C impairs terminal CIV maturation, prevents incorporation of heart-specific isoforms, and destabilizes the respirasome organization. Notably, this defect causes a selective secondary failure of complex I completion, demonstrating that respirasome formation is required for catalytic CI maturation in vivo. Consequently, cardiac-specific COX7C deficiency fails to complete the perinatal metabolic transition, leading to the collapse of fatty acid oxidation, activation of nucleotide and serine-glycine-one-carbon metabolism, attenuated activation of the mitochondrial integrated stress response, and a metabolically and structurally compromised state unlikely to support the increasing energetic demands of the postnatal heart. Together, these findings define a developmentally timed, CIV-dependent assembly step that couples respiratory chain assembly to postnatal cardiac metabolic fate and provide a temporal framework for mitochondrial maturation in the developing heart.

papers.title: Fathers' Relationship Satisfaction and Children's Mental Health During School Transition: The Role of Paternal Warmth and Family Socioeconomic Status.
papers.abstract: Despite extensive literature on discrete interparental adversities from mothers' perspectives, fathers' experiences of normative variation in couple functioning remained understudied. Using data from 8,186 father-child dyads in the Longitudinal Study of Australian Children, we examined fathers' relationship satisfaction and children's mental health across the preschool-to-primary-school transition, and explored the role of paternal warmth and family socioeconomic status (SES) during this process. Path analysis showed that paternal warmth at ages 6-7 was associated with fewer mental health difficulties in children at ages 8-9, beyond both parents' earlier warmth, mothers' relationship satisfaction, and children's difficulties at ages 4-5. Fathers' relationship satisfaction was associated with concurrent and subsequent paternal warmth but not with change in warmth once baseline warmth was controlled, providing limited evidence of longitudinal spillover. We found no evidence that SES moderated any longitudinal path. Our findings highlight paternal warmth during school transition as a potential intervention target for supporting children's mental health.

papers.title: Mixed-spectrum disturbance rejection during constrained fast-steering-mirror scan tracking.
papers.abstract: Scan tracking in space-telescope image stabilization requires the rejection of both slowly varying and narrow-band disturbances under coupled actuator constraints. We develop a shared-innovation hybrid generalized extended-state observer (hybrid-GESO) combined with model predictive control (MPC) that enforces coupled displacement-command limits for three lead zirconate titanate (PZT) actuators. The observer estimates low-frequency and resonant disturbance components and predicts their evolution over the MPC horizon. The dominant narrow-band disturbance frequency is assumed to be known a priori and approximately stationary during each scan. In five physical closed-loop experiments under combined slow and 5 Hz disturbances, hybrid-GESO-MPC achieved a mean radial root-mean-square (RMS) tracking error of 1.738±0.020 pixels, compared with 2.073±0.027 pixels for MPC with a linear extended-state observer (LESO-MPC), the best-performing selected baseline (mean±standard deviation, n=5). This corresponds to a 16.2% reduction.

papers.title: Comparing the Validity of Commonly Used Risk Assessment Tools in Men With Dual Histories of IPV and Sexual Offending.
papers.journal: Sexual abuse : a journal of research and treatment
papers.abstract: Individuals with dual histories of sexual and intimate partner violence (IPV) offending represent a complex subgroup, yet little is known about how well offence-specific risk assessment tools work for them. This field validity study compared the discrimination of an IPV risk tool (Spousal Assault Risk Assessment-Version 2; SARA-V2) with two sexual offending risk tools (Static-99R and STABLE-2007, as well as their combined risk level) in 467 men in British Columbia with dual sexual-IPV offending histories. The sexual offending measures predicted sexual recidivism with small to moderate effects, IPV recidivism with small effects, and violent recidivism with small to moderate effects. SARA-V2 total scores predicted IPV and violent recidivism with small effects but failed to predict sexual recidivism. Confidence intervals for all effects overlapped, indicating the measures had comparable discrimination. The Static-99R and Static/STABLE were the most broadly relevant in incremental validity analyses, predicting all three outcomes over and above the SARA-V2, while results for the STABLE-2007 were mixed. The SARA-V2 added predictive value to the Static-99R and STABLE-2007 for IPV and violent recidivism and to the Static/STABLE for violent recidivism. Given the SARA-V2's risk management benefits, our findings support using the Static-99R or Static/STABLE alongside the SARA-V2 for dual sexual-IPV offending subgroups.
